intro: [EXAMPLE] A light week: one puzzle, one conversation practice, your photography idea, and a film. Do any, all, or none.

items.title: Birthday problem, then break it
items.description: Derive the probability that two of n people share a birthday. Then find which assumption fails in real data and how that changes the answer.
items.why: Practises deriving instead of recalling, and questioning assumptions, the same move as critiquing an evaluation.
hints: Compute the probability that nobody shares a birthday.
Write it as a product of (365-k)/365 terms.
Use 1 - x <= e^{-x} to get a clean approximation. what n gives 1/2?
items.then: Explain the surprising answer to a friend in two minutes.
steps: Compute the probability that no two of n people share a birthday
Find n where it drops below 1/2
Look up real birth-date data and see which assumption breaks

items.title: Why does a random walk return home in 2D but not 3D?
items.description: Placeholder question. A real package asks a specific maths or physics question to think about.
hints: Compare the sum of 1/n with the sum of n to the minus 3/2.

items.title: The Library of Alexandria: what was really lost?
items.description: Placeholder talking point. A real package tells a history or philosophy story worth discussing.

items.title: One conversation where you only ask questions
items.description: In one real conversation this week, resist giving advice. Ask questions, and reflect back what you heard before responding.
items.why: Making people feel understood is mostly listening. This is a small, safe rep.
steps: Ask at least three open questions
Afterwards, note one thing you learned about the person
items.then: Afterwards, write one sentence on what you noticed about the other person.

items.title: Photo walk: only light and shadow
items.description: Your idea, scoped as a first experience: a 45-minute walk with your phone, photographing only interesting light.
items.why: You said you want to learn photography. A first experience tells you whether to make it a monthly skill project.
steps: Go out in the hour before sunset

items.title: Watch a film by a director you have never seen
items.description: Placeholder culture item. A real package names a specific film, with why it's worth your time.

reflection_prompt: Optional: what kind of activity gave you energy this week?

lessons.title: [EXAMPLE] Asking where something is
lessons.explanation: Use 〜はどこですか (… wa doko desu ka) to ask where something is. Replace … with the place.

questions.question: Ask where the hotel (ホテル) is.
Ask where the bank (銀行, ginkō) is.
questions.answer: 銀行はどこですか (ginkō wa doko desu ka)

practice: Say each example aloud, then ask Claude to role-play giving you directions.

lessons.title: [EXAMPLE] Greetings
lessons.explanation: నమస్కారం (namaskāram) is a respectful hello. ఎలా ఉన్నారు? (elā unnāru?) asks 'how are you?' politely.

questions.question: Ask someone politely how they are.

practice: Greet one Telugu speaker this week, or practise the exchange aloud with Claude.
